data.content_ref: inline:The target's distinguishing test itself cannot separate genuine reliability gain from mere compliance. By the target's own countercondition #2, panelists can get both intermediate and final items right for a wrong causal reason (common-cause confound), which inflates conditional dependence without genuine discrimination. Since the proposed mechanism relies entirely on detecting conditional dependence as its signal for 'genuine discrimination,' the test produces a false positive exactly in the case the problem asks it to rule out: compliance that merely tracks the right answer. The target acknowledges this vulnerability but provides no second-order test to disambiguate, so the single-evaluation evidence it offers is indeterminate between genuine reasoning and confounded compliance.
